title: Temples and towns along the Nile
standfirst: A Nile cruise between Luxor and Aswan stops at a handful of places, each with its own temple and character. Here they are in the order you meet them, sailing upstream.

sections.heading: From Luxor to Aswan
paragraphs: Luxor, the ancient city of Thebes, holds more monuments than anywhere else on the river. Upstream come Esna, with its lock and temple; Edfu, with the most complete temple to survive in Egypt; Kom Ombo, with its double temple on the riverbank; and Aswan, where the river runs between granite islands.
South of Aswan, Abu Simbel stands on the shore of Lake Nasser, most often visited as a day trip from Aswan.

sections.heading: How a cruise visits them
paragraphs: Ships stop at the main sites with guided visits, usually early in the day. Dahabiyas add smaller places between Esna and Aswan, such as El Kab and Gebel Silsila.

faqs.q: Which places does every cruise visit?
faqs.a: Between Luxor and Aswan, almost every cruise visits Luxor, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Aswan. Abu Simbel is an optional extra from Aswan.

seoTitle: Nile cruise stops: temples and towns
seoDescription: The temples and towns a Nile cruise visits between Luxor and Aswan, in river order, and Abu Simbel beyond.
